title: Logical replication, and replicating selectively between versions

videos.script: A standby is a copy of every byte, in the same version, and it cannot be written to. That is what makes it a good standby and a poor upgrade. {{bytes}} Logical replication sends rows instead. It names the tables, and the server receiving them can run another version. {{rows}} You publish the shop from your PostgreSQL 16, and subscribe to it from a PostgreSQL 17 in a container. {{subscribe}} Then you find what rows do not carry: a new column stops the subscription, and a sequence stays at one. {{gaps}} You offer one city's customers and nothing else. {{filter}} And you move to the 17 in five steps, which is an upgrade measured in minutes. {{switch}}
